436535.why: Van Gogh painted a restless, swirling sky over a calm golden field.

435809.why: Bruegel's harvesters eat, nap and work under a hazy late-summer sky, and nobody is in a rush.

437869.why: Velazquez painted his assistant Juan de Pareja looking straight back at you with quiet, unshakable dignity.

437881.why: Vermeer caught a woman alone at a window in the first soft light of the day, and nothing else needs to happen.

436105.why: David's Socrates keeps talking, calm and certain, while the people who love him fall apart around him.

437394.why: Rembrandt's Aristotle rests a hand on Homer's head and thinks about what lasts, in gold light and deep shadow.

435844.why: Caravaggio crowded four young musicians into one warm room, half tuning up and half daydreaming.

436839.why: La Tour's Magdalen sits alone with a single candle, letting a hard thought settle.

437549.why: Ruisdael gives you a wide road, ripe wheat and a sky that takes up most of the picture.

435888.why: Chardin's boy is giving all of his attention to one soap bubble, and for a moment so are you.

436545.why: Goya's little boy in red stands very still while the cats watch his pet magpie. Tender, and a bit uneasy.

437926.why: Watteau's Mezzetin plays his guitar to someone who has already turned away. Sweet, sad and a little funny.

435839.why: Canaletto's Piazza San Marco is full of people going somewhere, under a sky that has just cleared.

437397.why: Rembrandt at fifty-four, looking at himself without flattery and without flinching.

436101.why: Gerard David's holy family stops to rest on a long journey. The grass is soft and the day is kind.

437329.why: Poussin's Sabine Women is all motion and noise, every figure pulling in a different direction.

436282.why: Van Eyck fit a whole crowded world into two small panels, every face and cloud painted as if it mattered.

438817.why: Degas caught a dance class between exercises: fidgeting, stretching, whispering, waiting to begin.

436947.why: Manet's Boating is a bright afternoon on the water with someone you like and nowhere to be.

438815.why: Renoir painted a mother, two children and a very patient dog in a room that feels like home.

436534.why: Van Gogh painted these roses in his last spring, in the week he left the asylum, and they are pure relief.

436528.why: Van Gogh's irises push up against a yellow wall, every one of them a little different and all of them alive.

435868.why: Cezanne's card players have said everything they need to say. Two people, one table, total concentration.

438417.why: Friedrich's two friends stand in the dark and look at the moon together, saying nothing.

437854.why: Turner's whalers are barely there, swallowed by spray and weather. A storm you can feel in your chest.

438814.why: Delacroix painted a rescue in the middle of a burning castle, all hot color and panic.

437654.why: Seurat's sideshow is a crowd at night, lit by gas lamps, waiting to be let in. Quiet, strange, together.

437430.why: Renoir sat a friend in a wicker chair by the sea and let the whole afternoon go soft around her.

436532.why: Van Gogh painted himself in a straw hat because he could not afford a model, in quick, nervous strokes of yellow.

437097.why: Millet's haystacks sit in the last warm light of autumn, with the shepherd and his flock already heading home.

435702.why: Rosa Bonheur's Horse Fair is sixteen feet of muscle, dust and shouting. It is impossible to stand still in front of it.

436095.why: Daumier's third-class carriage is tired strangers pressed together, each lost in their own thoughts.

438821.why: Gauguin moved the Annunciation to Tahiti and filled it with fruit, flowers and heat.

435962.why: Corot's Hagar is at the end of her strength in an empty landscape, and help is just arriving.

437835.why: Toulouse-Lautrec caught an Englishman at the Moulin Rouge mid-flirt, in a room that is all noise and color.
